Welcome
Welcome to Little Acorns! We are a nonprofit early learning program serving children from 6
weeks through 5 years old, with after-school care for children up to age 12 at our Austin
location. We believe children learn best through play, relationships and a safe, predictable
day. This handbook explains how our centers work and what you can expect from us. Please
read it, keep it handy, and sign the acknowledgment on the last page.

Hours and Closings
Our centers are open Monday through Friday, 7:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., all year except for the
following holidays: New Year's Day, Memorial Day, Independence Day, Labor Day,
Thanksgiving Day and the day after, Christmas Eve and Christmas Day. We also close for two
staff training days each year, announced at least 30 days in advance.
If we must close because of severe weather, we will send a message through our parent app
and post on our website by 6:00 a.m.

Enrollment
To enroll, families complete our registration form, the enrollment agreement, an emergency
contact and authorized pickup form, and the child's health and immunization record.
Enrollment is complete once all forms are received and the registration fee is paid. We admit
children without regard to race, religion, national origin, sex or disability, and we make
reasonable accommodations for children with special needs.

Health Screenings
Depending on your child's age, state rules may require proof of vision and hearing screening
at enrollment. We'll tell you which screenings apply and help you find free screening events if
you need them.

Insurance
Little Acorns carries general liability insurance at each of our centers. A certificate of
insurance is available from the director on request.

Tuition and Fees
Tuition is billed monthly and is due on the 1st of each month through autopay. A late fee of
$25 applies to payments received after the 5th. Tuition is not reduced for absences, holidays
or closings. We accept child care subsidy, and families receiving subsidy pay only their
assigned parent fee. Please give us two weeks' written notice before withdrawing your child.

Arrival and Pickup
Please walk your child into the classroom and sign them in on the tablet at the front desk. A
staff member must greet your child before you leave.
We release children only to parents and to adults listed on the child's authorized pickup form.
We will ask for photo ID from anyone we don't recognize. If someone not on the list needs to
pick up your child, please call the director in advance and add them in writing. We will not
release a child to an adult who appears to be impaired; in that case we will call the other
parent or an emergency contact.
Late pickup. If you are running late, please call us. A late pickup fee of $1 per minute applies
after 6:00 p.m. If a child has not been picked up by 6:30 p.m. and we cannot reach any parent
or emergency contact, we will contact local law enforcement.

A Day at Little Acorns

Each day includes indoor and outdoor play, circle time, small-group activities, meals and rest.
Children play outside at least twice a day unless the weather is dangerous. Screen time is
limited to occasional educational programs.
Physical activity. Active play helps children grow strong, sleep well and learn. Every day,
children have time for running, climbing, dancing and ball games, both outdoors on our
playground and indoors in our movement room when the weather keeps us in. Teachers lead
at least two short active games each day and join in the play.
Sunscreen and insect repellent. With your written permission, we apply the sunscreen
you provide before outdoor play, and insect repellent when needed. Products must be labeled
with your child's name. We don't apply sunscreen or repellent to babies under 6 months.
Water play and animals. We don't offer swimming or wading pools. Children may play at
a water table with a teacher present. We don't keep classroom pets; if a visitor brings an
animal, we tell families in advance.

Rest and Safe Sleep
Children 12 months and older rest on individual cots after lunch for up to two hours. Children
who don't sleep may read quietly.
Infants sleep in individual cribs, following their own schedules. Babies are placed on their
backs to sleep, with no blankets, pillows or toys in the crib. To avoid waking a baby, infants
who fall asleep in a bouncer, swing or car seat may finish their nap there as long as a teacher
can see them.

Guidance and Discipline
We use positive guidance: clear expectations, redirection, praise and natural consequences.
We never use spanking, shaking or any physical punishment, and we never shame or yell at
children. When a child needs a break, a teacher may offer a short time-out in the classroom,
about one minute per year of age, with the teacher nearby. Children who throw food or refuse
to sit at lunch may lose their dessert for that day.

Meals and Allergies
We serve breakfast, lunch and an afternoon snack that meet USDA nutrition guidelines. The
daily menu, including all meals and snacks, is posted at the entrance of each center. Please tell

us in writing about any food allergy. For children with a severe allergy, we need an allergy
action plan signed by the child's health care provider before the child's first day.

Illness
To keep everyone healthy, please keep your child home if they have a fever of 100.4°F or
higher, vomiting, diarrhea, an unexplained rash, or are too sick to take part in normal
activities. If your child becomes ill at the center, we will call you and you must pick up within
one hour. Children may return when they have been fever-free for 24 hours without medicine.

Medication
We can give prescription and over-the-counter medicine during the day when it is necessary.
Medicine must be in its original container, labeled with your child's name. To make things
easier for busy families, you may authorize medication by phone or by text message to your
child's teacher, and we will note your permission in the medication log. We record every dose
we give.

Injuries and Emergencies
Every classroom has a first aid kit. All teachers and the director hold current pediatric first aid
certification, and at least one staff member with current pediatric CPR certification is at each
center whenever children are present. If your child has a minor injury, we will tell you at
pickup and give you a written incident report. For a serious injury we will call 911 first and
then call you right away.
We practice a fire drill every month, and children learn to leave the building quickly and
calmly. We also practice shelter-in-place and lockdown drills several times a year. Our
evacuation map is posted in every classroom.

Field Trips
Older children sometimes walk to the park or library near the center. We'll let you know about
walking trips on the morning of the trip. For trips by bus, we'll ask you to sign a permission
slip.

Child Abuse and Neglect

We take children's safety very seriously. If a staff member suspects that a child has been
abused or neglected, they tell the center director, who looks into the concern and decides
whether to contact child protective services.

Records and Privacy
Your child's records are confidential and are shared only with you, our staff and licensing
staff. We keep attendance and children's records for at least three years after a child leaves our
program, or longer if state rules require it.

Communication and Visiting
Parents are welcome to visit at any time during our hours, without calling first. We share
updates through our parent app and hold parent-teacher conferences twice a year.
Your rights as a parent. You have the right to visit your child at any time we are open, to
see your child's records, to see our most recent licensing inspection report (posted at the
entrance), and to contact the state licensing agency with any concern about our program. We
will never take action against a family for raising a concern.
Questions and concerns. We want to hear from you. Please talk with your child's teacher
first; if your concern isn't resolved, ask for a meeting with the center director, who will meet
with you within three business days. You may also contact your state's child care licensing
office at any time. The office's phone number is posted at the entrance.
